decision: PENDING the user's batched official evaluation. This candidate exists to collect an official full-package reading for A-GR1, whose official value (+29) was measured by side isolation and has never been landed on a complete root. Both halves of the promotion rule are fixed here before the number arrives: an official score above the current root's 18518 inside 300s promotes it; a timeout or a lower score does not.

sibling_evidence_recorded_after_archivin.event: the v234 complete package (v230 root + the same A-GR1 block) was reported by the user as an official TIMEOUT (>300s) on 2026-09-10, after this card was built and archived
sibling_evidence_recorded_after_archivin.impact_on_this_candidate: A-GR1's extra cost is calibration-side and is a property of the mechanism, not of the Linear parent; v231 is only 1s faster than v230 (291s vs 292s). So this candidate's expected total is about v234's minus 1s, and it fits inside 300s only if v234's overshoot was at most 1s. The overshoot magnitude is unknown.
sibling_evidence_recorded_after_archivin.effect_on_the_preregistered_rule: none -- the rule is unchanged. The evidence makes its timeout branch the likely one; it does not settle this SHA, because this is a different implementation (different parent) and the overshoot magnitude was never reported.
sibling_evidence_recorded_after_archivin.no_prediction: no seconds and no score are predicted here; the exact overshoot is unknown and side time has no calibrated relationship to the complete package.

side_isolation_reference.note: the +29 is a side-isolation measurement on the v234 source, which is byte-identical to this candidate in its Attention section. Side score does not promote and side time does not predict the full package.

time_risk: A-GR1 adds calibration-side training. The side probe measured +20.7s against the v195 side, and the current complete root sits at 291s against the 300s limit (9s of headroom). The sibling v234 complete package, with 8s of headroom and the same calibration-side cost, was then reported as an official TIMEOUT. Side time has no calibrated relationship to the full package, so the only way to learn this candidate's real number is an official reading; the submission's expected value is now low and the user may reasonably decide not to spend it. A timeout closes this implementation only.
recommended_next_attention_action: the evidence now says the block on A-GR1 is time headroom (about 20s is needed against 9s available), not the parent and not the mechanism. The highest-value Attention work is therefore to reclaim calibration/complete-package seconds first -- the same direction the Linear runtime cards (v233 L-TF1, already officially priced at -4s, and v235 L-AD1) are taking -- and only then land A-GR1. Re-running A-GR1 variants is not a route: weakening it (fewer steps, fewer windows, fewer candidates) is forbidden by the card's own rules.
